newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria stands to win $6 bln from gas transit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria stands to win $6 bln from gas transit.

text.p: Bulgaria stands to gain $5.8 billion net revenue over 30 years from a pipeline concession for transiting Russian gas through its territory, if the government grants the concession, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Lobov said on Tuesday.
Lobov discussed with Bulgaria's Prime Minister Zhan Videnov bilateral economic projects and the long-delayed pipeline concession during a one-day visit.
"The joint gas distribution company is expected to yield net revenue of $5.8 billion over a 30-year period of operation," Lobov told a news conference.

In mid-July the Bulgarian cabinet decided to open a procedure for granting a concession to Bulgarian-Russian joint stock company Topenergy, which was set up in 1995 by Russian gas monopoly RAO Gazprom and Bulgarian gas monopolist Bulgargas.
A decision is expected to be taken in the next weeks during a visit Gazprom president Rem Viakhirev, said Lobov.
"Then it will take three more months to regulate pricing issues, but we hope this period can be shortened to two months at the most," said Lobov.
Cash-strapped Bulgaria stands to receive $100 million net revenue in the first year of the operation of the project, he said.

After enlarging the system to accomodate growing demand in neighbouring Serbia, Greece, Turkey, Macedonia and Albania, which is estimated to cost $500 million, the joint venture is expected to supply some 30 billion cubic metres of gas by year 2010.
"It is necessary to act quickly as a new gas and oil pipeline project directly under the Black Sea is gaining speed," said Lobov.
However head of Bulgaria's concession department Nikolai Baltov did not confirm the time frame announced by Lobov.

"Negotiations concern agreeing on fixed supply prices instead of floating ones...Agreeing on these and other issues may take a long time as they concern serious corporate interests," Baltov told journalists.

Bulgaria has a 2,200-km pipeline network, including 625 km of transit pipelines which receive and transmit gas from outside the country. Bulgaria supplies Turkey with three bcm of gas per year and started supplying some gas to Greece last month. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
